findings.evidence: `grep -n 'lean_source' code/scripts` → `check-expired-upstream-shims.py:25: from lean_source import qualified_declarations, strip_comments_and_strings`; `lean_source.py:167 def strip_comments_and_strings`, `:326 def declarations`, `:461 def qualified_declarations`.
findings.fix: Build the index from `lean_source.qualified_declarations(text)` (it gives the names, the count, and the EpsilonEridani-vs-upstream split), and add a `keep_docs` option to `lean_source.strip_comments_and_strings` for the roadmap bodies rather than keeping a second stripper. Keep only the genuinely new parsers here (`parse_imports`, `opened_namespaces`, `layer_sections`), which lean_source does not cover.
findings.issue: `declarations` (line 173) and `strip_comments` (line 96) duplicate `scripts/lean_source.py`'s `strip_comments_and_strings`, `declarations`/`scopes`/`update_scope` and `qualified_declarations` as a weaker line-anchored copy; module_graph.py imports only `chart_style` (line 49). Two parsers for the same question ('which declarations does this module define') will diverge, so the published graph's declaration index, `decls` counts and `upstream_namespace` flags can contradict the repo's own shim and dot-notation checks.

findings.evidence: `grep -n 'used_by_roadmaps|pins|public|meta\b|n\.path' code/scripts/module_graph.{py,html}` → the only html hits are `<meta charset>`, `<meta name=viewport>`, the `.meta` CSS class and `location.pathname`; `to_dot` (line 460) reads only `id`, `label`, `url`, `dir`/`area`/`package`, `upstream_namespace`, `kind`, `redundant`.
findings.fix: Drop these fields (and the `used_by_roadmaps` loop and the `public`/`meta` capture groups that feed them), or surface them in the viewer — e.g. mark `meta`/`public` imports in the side panel and show `pins` next to the entry-point links.
findings.issue: Fields computed and shipped in the ~360 KB published JSON with no reader: per-edge `public`/`meta` (line 410, on every import edge), node `path` (line 396), `used_by_roadmaps` (lines 434-436, a whole pass over nodes), and top-level `pins` (line 444). The viewer recomputes `linked` from the roadmap edges instead of using `used_by_roadmaps`, and the dot renderer uses none of these.

summary: The generator re-implements, at a weaker line-based level, the Lean source parsing that scripts/lean_source.py already provides and that another script already reuses, so the published graph can disagree with the repo's own tooling about what a module declares. It also emits several JSON fields no consumer reads.
